objectives:
"At the end of the semester, students are expected to achieve followings.

(1) fundamental programming skills for scientific data analysis,
(2) knowledge on ways to read and use widely used astronomical catalogues,
(3) basic analysis techniques such as least-squares fitting and periodicity analysis,
(4) basic knowledge on SQL language and use of database management system,
(5) semi-automated classification techniques using machine learning."
content:
"This course focuses on practical programming skills required to carry out astronomical research. The official computer language for this course is Python. Topics for this course include, but not limited to, (1) retrieval of astronomical catalogues, such as astrometric cataglogues of stars and asteroid orbital elements catalogues, and fundamental usage of those catalogues, (2) data visualization techniques to produce research-grade quality plots, such as scatter plots, histograms, and contour maps, (3) basic data analysis techniques, such as least-squares fitting and periodicity analysis, (4) construction of relational databases and usage of those databases by SQL language, (5) semi-automated classification techniques using machine learning. This course is offered in hands-on session style. Students who take this course need to bring their own computer to the classroom. Sample programs written in Python are provided. Students first make programs exactly same as those sample programs to learn how it works. Then, students start to work on number of exercises.

This course is primarily for graduate students of master and doctor courses.
It is also open for highly motivated undergraduate students who are interested in analysis of astronomical data and catalogues."
